title: Why Does an F1 Steering Wheel Have So Many Buttons?
description:
The steering wheel of a Formula One car has more than twenty buttons, dials and switches, a screen in the middle and paddles behind it. And the driver uses them at three hundred kilometres per hour, with one thumb, between corners. It is not a steering wheel. It is the control room of the car. Today, ten parts of the F1 cockpit, and why each one exists, starting with the wheel.

Machine Reverse takes apart the machines you see every day and explains, part by part, why each one exists. This video covers 10 parts.

Chapters:
0:00 Intro
1:12 1. The steering wheel
2:41 2. The rotary dials
3:58 3. The paddles
5:13 4. The quick release
6:24 5. The lights on the wheel
7:41 6. The drink button
9:01 7. The extraction seat
10:14 8. The HANS device
11:34 9. The race suit
12:59 10. The biometric gloves
14:20 The verdict
